Write a polynomial-time reduction from 3-SAT to Independent Set. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is 3-SAT and TARGET is Independent Set. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = ThreeSat
3-SAT.

Instance: {"num_vars": m, "clauses": [[l1, l2, l3], ...]}
  * Variables are 1..m. A literal is +v (v is true) or -v (v is false).
  * Every clause has exactly 3 literals on 3 different variables, so a
    clause may not repeat a variable or contain both v and -v.
  * Literal order inside a clause and clause order do not matter. The
    same clause may appear more than once.
  * Variables need not all appear in a clause.

Yes iff some assignment of true/false to variables 1..m makes every
clause contain at least one true literal.

Edge cases: a formula with no clauses is satisfiable (yes), for any m,
including m = 0. A formula with clauses needs m >= 3.

TARGET = IndependentSet
Independent Set.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has an independent set of AT LEAST k vertices: k
vertices with no edge between any two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k > n is always no. With no edges,
every set of vertices is independent.

WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-fkajprv_

    reduce(instance) -> instance

The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

{"command":"cd /tmp/reduction-fkajprv_ && cat <<'EOF' > reduce.py
"""Polynomial-time reduction from 3-SAT to Independent Set.

Construction
------------
For every literal occurrence in every clause we create one vertex.  The
vertices belonging to the same clause form a triangle, so an independent set
can pick at most one literal from each clause.  For every pair of vertices
whose literals are complementary (v and -v) we add an edge, so an independent
set may not pick both a variable and its negation.

The target instance asks for an independent set of size at least
k = number of clauses.  Any satisfying assignment yields such a set by picking
one true literal per clause (the triangles forbid two picks in one clause, and
the consistency edges forbid picking both v and -v).  Conversely, any
independent set of size k picks exactly one literal per clause and never both
a variable and its negation; setting those literals to true satisfies every
clause.

A formula with no clauses maps to the empty graph with k = 0, which is a yes
instance, matching the 3-SAT edge case.
"""


def reduce(instance):
    """Reduce a 3-SAT instance to an Independent Set instance."""
    clauses = instance["clauses"]

    edges = set()
    vertex = 0
    # vertex -> literal it represents
    literals = []

    for clause in clauses:
        base = vertex
        for literal in clause:
            literals.append(literal)
            vertex += 1
        # Triangle on the three literal vertices of this clause.
        edges.add((base, base + 1))
        edges.add((base, base + 2))
        edges.add((base + 1, base + 2))

    # Consistency edges between complementary literals in different clauses.
    by_literal = {}
    for index, literal in enumerate(literals):
        by_literal.setdefault(literal, []).append(index)
    for literal, indices in by_literal.items():
        for other in by_literal.get(-literal, ()):
            for i in indices:
                for j in other:
                    if i != j:
                        edges.add((i, j) if i < j else (j, i))

    return {
        "n": vertex,
        "edges": [[u, v] for u, v in sorted(edges)],
        "k": len(clauses),
    }
EOF

    edges = instance.get("edges")
    require(isinstance(edges, list), "edges must be a list")
    seen: set[frozenset[int]] = set()
    for edge in edges:

        require(0 <= u < n and 0 <= v < n, f"edge {edge!r} has a vertex outside 0..{n - 1}")
        require(u != v, f"self-loop {edge!r} is not allowed")
        key = frozenset((u, v))
        require(key not in seen, f"duplicate edge {edge!r}")
        seen.add(key)

    for clause in clauses:

def all_graphs(n: int) -> Iterator[list[list[int]]]:
    """Every labelled simple graph on n vertices, as an edge list.
    There are 2^(n(n-1)/2) of them: 1,024 at n = 5, 32,768 at n = 6."""
    pairs = list(combinations(range(n), 2))
    for mask in range(1 << len(pairs)):
        yield [list(pair) for index, pair in enumerate(pairs) if mask >> index & 1]


def random_graph(rng: random.Random, n: int, p: float | None = None) -> list[list[int]]:
    """Edge list with each edge present with probability p (random if None)."""
    p = rng.random() if p is None else p
    return [[u, v] for u, v in combinations(range(n), 2) if rng.random() < p]
